title: Preimage Size of Factorial Zeroes Function
summary: Define f(x) as the count of trailing zeroes in the factorial of x.
statement: Define f(x) as the count of trailing zeroes in the factorial of x. For instance, f(3) equals 0 since 3! equals 6, which has no trailing zeroes, whereas f(11) equals 2 because 11! equals 39916800, which has two trailing zeroes. Given an integer k, determine the count of non-negative integers x for which f(x) equals k.
constraints: Let f(x) be the number of trailing zeros in x factorial.
Count nonnegative integers x satisfying f(x)=k.
Return the preimage size, which is either zero or five.
hints: Trailing-zero count is monotone in x.
Binary-search the first x with f(x)>=target.
The values with f(x)=k lie between lower(k) and lower(k+1).
Subtracting those boundary indices gives the exact count without enumerating large factorials.
editorial: Subtracting those boundary indices gives the exact count without enumerating large factorials.

tests.explanation: Values zero through four have no factorial trailing zeros, so return five.
No factorial has exactly five trailing zeros, so return zero.
